published_hypotheses: As READ in arXiv v1 (the same paper, pre-proof): flat Minkowski background; free massless minimally coupled scalar field; all quadratic and quartic operators normal-ordered with respect to the Minkowski vacuum (v1 p.5, after (3.2)); coincidence limit, 00 component (Delta defined pointwise by (3.2) with an absolute value); single-mode vacuum+two-particle and squeezed states, Casimir vacuum between plates; Wick's theorem for states with phi+|psi> = <psi|phi- = 0 (Sec. III.C); Delta proposed as 'a measure' of semiclassical validity; curved-space extension explicitly requires an undeveloped quartic renormalisation (Sec. V).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. KF's content is algebra in flat spacetime with no measured input (data_at_publication row 1): no datum they lacked could move (2.16), (3.7), (3.8) or the inequality after (3.8) -- those stand or fall by computation, and the computation here (A1-A11) is exact and data-free. What KF lacked in 1993 was THEORY, not data, and they said so: 'a renormalization procedure for quartic operator products in such [curved] spacetimes, which has not yet been developed' (v1 Sec. V, READ via d67/src/gr-qc_9304008.note). That gap has since been addressed by OPE methods (2512.17789, READ) and the criterion itself refined by back-reaction arguments (gr-qc/0402029, READ) and contested on the normal-ordering choice (1807.03808, READ) -- each narrows the reach of Delta as a validity criterion; none refutes KF's flat-space qualitative finding, and gr-qc/9410043 (READ) restates that finding as standing. For THIS entry -- the journal version -- the missing item is not physical data but the journal text itself, which could not be reached here (quota / egress). Evidence against M's hypothesis for this entry: nothing in KF depends on a measured constant. Evidence for 'incomplete': the curved-space and smearing gaps, stated by KF themselves. Nothing here says the journal is wrong, and nothing says it repeats v1's slips.
grade_evidence: The journal text, PRD 47, 4510-4519 (1993), is NAMED-NOT-READ in this audit: every route was refused (alphaXiv quota exceeded x4; journals.aps.org, arxiv.org, pubmed, doi.org, crossref, inspirehep egress-blocked). Its equations therefore cannot be checked here, and under M's rule a claim that cannot be checked is OPEN, not STANDS or WRONG. What IS established, both ways: (i) the tree's use of this entry is a scope clause and it is exact -- JOURNAL_VERSION_READ = False, the docstring's NAMED-NOT-READ and MUST-NOT clause, SOURCE scoped to v1, ledger.py's consistency raise, and no file under research/warp-drive asserting an error in the journal (T1-T6); (ii) the v1 discrepancies the clause protects are real and reproducible (A1-A11: (2.16) final = 1/2 exact; (3.7) off by 1/(1+eps^2); exact Delta 0.5134 vs (3.8) 2.0118 at the witness; z3: rho<0 => 1/3 < Delta < 1, so 'Delta > 1' fails everywhere on rho<0 in v1) -- so the clause is protecting findings, not artefacts; (iii) v1 (6 Apr 1993) is a pre-proof manuscript ~5-6 weeks before the May 1993 issue, so proof corrections are possible and undetermined; one WebSearch found no erratum, which is not evidence of none. Nothing here moves any ledger row; nothing is in M's favour.
